note: Forest Service campground on Marble Creek off Highway E between Fredericktown and Arcadia, beside the old grist-mill dam and the Marble Creek trailhead of the Ozark Trail; remote, with no cell service. Shaded sites along the road down the hill to the loop; the six downhill-side sites at the bottom sit on a wooded slope above the creek with paths down to it. Creek access and the 4-ft mill pond are at the day-use area about 1/4 mile past the campground. --Claude
summary: Confirmed $15, FCFS (no rec.gov listing), 26 sites, vault toilets, no water; season now Apr 9 - Nov 1 (FS 2026). WATERFRONT DOWN creekside -> not waterfront (the six 'creekside' sites are on a wooded hill, 'shielded from view by trees'). Phone 573-438-5427 to add; pin ~130 m (optional).
flags: WATERFRONT DOWN (creekside -> not waterfront): Forest Service page: 'At the bottom of the hill, the 6 downhill side sites are located next to the creek. The Creekside sites are located on a hill, with paths from them that lead down to the creek. The sites are shielded from view by trees.' The FS does not number them. Imagery (180 m frame): the loop road at the bottom of the hill is ~50 m from the creek (channel ~20-25 m wide, so creekside-class, not river), and the ground between the downhill-side pads and the water is a dense wooded slope (pines) - no open apron for any of the six, and the FS itself says the trees screen the creek from the sites. None earns creekside under the 50 m open-apron rule; there is no creek-view value and the FS says the view is screened, so not waterfront.
